sections.overview: Lethrinus obsoletus (Forsskål, 1775) is a marine emperor in the family Lethrinidae.
sections.identification: It is olive to brown with an orange-yellow stripe along the lower flank and can reach about 60 centimetres total length.
sections.habitat: It ranges from the Red Sea and East Africa across the Indo-Pacific to the Ryukyu Islands and French Polynesia, using shallow reefs, lagoons, seagrass beds and nearby sand or rubble, usually to about 30 metres.
sections.diet: It feeds on bottom-dwelling molluscs, crustaceans and echinoderms.
sections.behavior: Adults may be solitary or occur in groups; juveniles are also recorded on weedy reefs.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific spawning details are limited in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Lethrinus with the drab emperor (L. ravus) and red snout emperor (L. reticulatus); their companion profiles make their different identifying patterns easy to compare.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment dated 2015 classified it as Least Concern.
